description:
Watch a whole video file with ffmpeg and get back its shots, pacing, black or frozen stretches and loudness. Use it twice in a film: on a reference film the user likes, to copy its shot count and rhythm, and on your own finished render, to fix it before the user watches.

This server runs on the user's machine: pass the file's absolute path and it returns the shot table, what to fix, and a contact sheet with one frame from each shot.

The numbers cannot see clipped words or overlaps. For those, look at the contact sheet or use render-video-frames.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

file.description: Absolute path of the video on this machine: a reference film to study, or your own render to check.

threshold.description: Scene score that counts as a change. Keep 0.05 for motion-design films; 0.3 finds only hard cuts.

name: watch-video
title: Watch a Video
